description.en: Build clean pulling, pushing, leg strength, trunk control, mobility, and resilient joints.
Develop pull-over control, high pulls, support strength, and assisted transitions.
Build controlled muscle-up transitions, tuck-lever foundations and supported handstand practice.
Repeat clean supported skills, strengthen tuck shapes and develop balanced full-body strength.
Develop longer-lever strength, controlled muscle-ups and handstand balance while maintaining full-body fundamentals and flexibility.
Strong basics, plus handstand, flag, lever and planche work at your level. Straddle shapes take most adults years: until one is clean, train the rung below for the same sets.
The straddle front lever, short full back levers and full flags, one-arm push-ups, shrimp squats and one-arm pull-up groundwork. Full shapes take most adults years: until then, train the rung below.
Long sets of the basics, and the full front lever, straddle planche, V-sit and deficit handstand push-ups join. Doses climb faster now. Miss an exam and repeat the block: that's how this level works.

Full levers become the main work. The full planche, one-arm pull-up, one-arm handstand and Hefesto begin, and the basics climb in steep steps. Repeating a block after a missed exam is part of the plan.
The last level: the top skills climb toward Elite, and it ends with the two Champion tests. Most athletes repeat blocks here, and the rung below is always in the class.

progression_readiness.en: Move up after two classes at this dose with full range, a controlled exit and reps to spare. Until then, stay on the easier version. Change one thing at a time.

training_recovery.en: Do the classes in order and keep the easy ones easy. Warm-up feels heavy? Walk and stretch today, then do the next class once rested.
